title: Essential constancy is invariant under initial restriction of pro-diagrams
statement: Let $H:\mathcal I\to\mathcal J$ be an initial functor between cofiltered categories and let $M:\mathcal J\to\mathcal C$ be a diagram in a category $\mathcal C$ [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. Then $M$ is essentially constant as a pro-object if and only if $M\circ H$ is essentially constant, with the same value. More precisely, if $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_j:X\to M(j)$, then $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_{H(i)}$; and if $M\circ H$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $v_i:X\to M(H(i))$, then $M$ is essentially constant with value $X$ and cone maps $u_j$ satisfying $u_{H(i)}=v_i$ for all $i$.

proof.text: Restriction directly from Definition 05PU(2). Choose p:H(i0)→j0 by initiality and use M(p)≫r as the retraction; naturality of u gives the splitting. For i choose the original factorization stage j and lift it by q:H(l)→j. Cofilteredness of I supplies a stage over i0, l, i. Apply Mathlib Functor.Initial.exists_eq twice, first to equalize the composites to j0, then those to H(i). Applying M and the original factorization proves the restricted common-stage clause. This is the proved private helper restrict_witness. The elementary refinement argument uses Mathlib Functor.initial_iff_of_isCofiltered and IsCofilteredOrEmpty.cone_objs.

Extend the given cone with Functor.Initial.extendCone, the cone-extension clause of [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit]. Mathlib extendCone_obj_π_app' gives u_j=v_i≫M(p) for any p:H(i)→j. In particular, taking the identity arrow shows u_{H(i)}=v_i. Keep j0=H(i0) and the given retraction. For each j choose p:H(i)→j by initiality and postcompose the factorization at i by M(p); the component formula yields the common-stage clause at j. This is the proved private helper extend_witness.

Unpack IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram and apply the preceding witness constructions in each direction. The restricted cone is explicitly the natural transformation with components u_{H(i)}. The same two constructions establish the prescribed-cone clauses. All values, cone components and universes remain unchanged.

lean.statement: theorem initial_iff_essentiallyConstantProDiagram {I : Type uI} {J : Type uJ} {C : Type uC} [Category.{vI} I] [Category.{vJ} J] [Category.{vC} C] [IsCofiltered I] [IsCofiltered J] (H : I ⥤ J) [H.Initial] (M : J ⥤ C) (X : C) : (IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram M X ↔ IsEssentiallyConstantProDiagram (H ⋙ M) X) ∧ (∀ u : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ M, (∃ j₀ : J, ∃ r : M.obj j₀ ⟶ X, u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ j : J, ∃ k : J, ∃ a : k ⟶ j₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ j, M.map b = M.map a ≫ r ≫ u.app j) → ∃ i₀ : I, ∃ r : M.obj (H.obj i₀) ⟶ X, u.app (H.obj i₀) ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ k : I, ∃ a : k ⟶ i₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ i, M.map (H.map b) = M.map (H.map a) ≫ r ≫ u.app (H.obj i)) ∧ (∀ v : (Functor.const I).obj X ⟶ H ⋙ M, (∃ i₀ : I, ∃ r : M.obj (H.obj i₀) ⟶ X, v.app i₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ k : I, ∃ a : k ⟶ i₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ i, M.map (H.map b) = M.map (H.map a) ≫ r ≫ v.app i) → ∃ u : (Functor.const J).obj X ⟶ M, (∃ j₀ : J, ∃ r : M.obj j₀ ⟶ X, u.app j₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 X ∧ ∀ j : J, ∃ k : J, ∃ a : k ⟶ j₀, ∃ b : k ⟶ j, M.map b = M.map a ≫ r ≫ u.app j) ∧ ∀ i : I, u.app (H.obj i) = v.app i)
